rule: These checks are deliberately not claimed by local unit tests. Execute them after pushing the repository and attach the terminal run's debug manifest and relevant redacted logs.
prerequisites: A target PC or target container matching the intended deployment
A real webpage MCP client supporting OAuth
HTTPS or an approved loopback development URL
A configured native isolation helper/container with no private-vault mount
A real LaTeX toolchain when RE_CTM_LATEX_POLICY=required
External theorem/web retrieval connectivity if used by the reasoning workflow

checks.name: OAuth discovery and dynamic registration
steps: Run Re-CTM on 127.0.0.1 without RE_CTM_SERVER_URL or RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD; record the generated Re-CTM OAuth authorization key shown only in the local operator terminal, then start a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel after the server is already listening and confirm no Re-CTM restart is needed when the random trycloudflare.com hostname appears.
Fetch OAuth authorization-server and protected-resource metadata through the Quick Tunnel and confirm issuer/resource/endpoint URLs use the public HTTPS trycloudflare.com origin.
Run scripts/smoke_oauth_mcp.py against the public base URL and save its redacted report.
Connect the webpage client to /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and the MCP URL.
Confirm DCR creates a client and the browser is redirected to /oauth/authorize.
Complete PKCE authorization and token exchange.
Repeat with an explicit RE_CTM_SERVER_URL and confirm forwarded Host headers cannot replace that fixed OAuth origin.
expected: No static bearer or no-auth path is offered.

When no OAuth password is configured, a high-entropy authorization key is generated for the serve session, displayed to the local operator, accepted on the first OAuth page, and absent from structured logs, reports, HTTP payloads, and persisted state.
Dynamic OAuth origin works only with a loopback-bound server and the tunnel's trusted local proxy request; non-loopback dynamic bind is rejected.
An access token issued for the public tunnel origin is rejected when replayed against a different effective origin.
The client reaches tools/list only with a valid OAuth access token.
Debug events contain fingerprints, not raw codes, secrets, passwords, or tokens.

checks.name: Fixed tool catalog across native modes and workflow states
steps: Confirm scripts/smoke_oauth_mcp.py reports exactly 31 tools (18 CTM Native + 13 Rethlas) and a modern non-inheritance result.
Capture tools/list in safe, trusted, and dangerous native modes.
Capture tools/list during generator, branch, join, verifier, and repair states.
expected: Catalog and schemas are identical.
Authorization changes server-side call results rather than catalog visibility.

checks.name: Dangerous native isolation
steps: Install bubblewrap on Linux or provide an independently reviewed external helper.
Run `re-ctm attest-native --backend bubblewrap --workspace <workspace> --data-root <data-root> --private-root <private-root>` without enabling native execution.

Run `python3 scripts/manual_native_isolation_test.py --backend bubblewrap --workspace <workspace> --data-root <data-root> --private-root <private-root> --output native-isolation-validation.json` and review every check.
Only after the report passes, run Re-CTM with native_mode=dangerous, RE_CTM_NATIVE_EXEC_BACKEND=bubblewrap, and the operator acknowledgement RE_CTM_NATIVE_ISOLATION_ATTESTED=1.
Use exec_command to enumerate mounts and attempt direct reads of the configured Re-CTM data/private roots.
Attempt privilege escalation, parent-environment recovery, namespace creation, and access through interpreters or nested shells.
expected: Native workspace remains usable.
Private run store is not mounted or otherwise reachable.
The helper response is nonce-bound and attests mount, user, PID, environment, capability, and network properties.
Safe mode has a private network namespace; trusted/dangerous network behavior matches the selected native policy.
Dangerous never grants a rethlas_* capability or finalization authority.

checks.name: Sequential branch-domain information barrier
steps: Create at least three materially different decomposition plans.
Execute branch A, seal it, then enter branch B and branch C.
Try rethlas_read against prior and future branch identifiers before join.
Enter join only after all branches are sealed.
expected: Every branch receives the same snapshot hash.
Cross-branch reads are denied until join.
Sealed capability reuse is denied.
Join receives all branch results simultaneously.

checks.name: Verifier data firewall and mechanical verdict
steps: Reach verifier state with a complete proof.tex.
Attempt to read generation memory, branch results, steering, and join internals.
Submit a report whose model-supplied verdict conflicts with its findings.
expected: All generation-private reads are denied.
Server computes correct only when critical_errors and gaps are both empty.
Wrong findings route to repair and cannot create proof_verified.tex.

checks.name: Browser disconnect, resume, steering, and cancellation
steps: Disconnect the webpage after a task is issued.
Reconnect with the same OAuth client and call rethlas_resume.
Queue steering and confirm it appears only at a safe generator/repair checkpoint.
Cancel another run and attempt further writes with its previous capability.
expected: State survives browser disconnect.
Steering is not exposed to verifier.
Cancelled run is sealed and previous capabilities fail.

checks.name: Real LaTeX gate and verified artifact
steps: Run on Linux with RE_CTM_LATEX_POLICY=required, bubblewrap, and a real latexmk installation.
Submit malformed, external-input, shell-escape, and valid self-contained documents.
Create a host-only readable LaTeX class or file outside the compiler scratch directory and confirm the proof cannot load it even by absolute path.
Complete a correct verification report for the valid document.
Call rethlas_export_final to a new workspace-relative .tex path, then retry the same path without expected_sha256 and confirm the overwrite is denied.
expected: Unsafe or uncompilable LaTeX routes to repair, and Re-CTM never falls back to compiling model-generated TeX directly on the host.
The compiler receives only a scratch workspace plus read-only system TeX/toolchain roots; Re-CTM private state is not mounted.
Only a compiled proof with empty findings reaches done.
The sole final delivery artifact is proof_verified.tex.
The controlled export writes exactly the finalized bytes inside the native workspace and refuses baseline-free overwrite.

checks.name: Rethlas methodology behavior acceptance
steps: Use representative easy, difficult, citation-heavy, counterexample-sensitive, and repair-requiring math problems.

Inspect memory channels, multiple plan generation, exact per-plan/per-subgoal direct screening, one-branch-per-plan work, all-branch join, failure synthesis, replanning, verification audits, and changed-proof repair.
Use rethlas_retrieve for nontrivial claims; for useful results, inspect the source paper context/proof and persist definitions, applicability checks, and identifiers before relying on them.
expected: Core Rethlas methodology is observably preserved despite sequential domains.
Failures remain queryable and influence new plans.
External results include complete statements and applicability checks.
Operator judges the target 95-percent functional-equivalence criterion.

checks.name: Coding Tools MCP 18-tool compatibility
steps: Capture tools/list from the reference Coding Tools MCP and Re-CTM, and compare the 18 CTM native names, order, required fields, enums, defaults, and annotations.
Exercise read_file, list_dir, list_files, search_text, apply_patch, Git tools, request_permissions, and view_image against the same disposable workspace.

With the Re-CTM bubblewrap backend enabled, run a long command that returns command_id, poll with write_stdin, page retained stdout/stderr with read_output, interact with a tty=true command, and terminate another command with kill_command.
Repeat command lifecycle checks in safe, trusted, and dangerous native modes and confirm dangerous does not grant any rethlas_* workflow capability.
expected: No CTM native tool is missing from Re-CTM; the fixed catalog is exactly 18 CTM native tools plus 13 Rethlas tools.
Existing CTM-style calls using patch envelopes and cmd/workdir command arguments remain accepted.
Long-running command IDs remain usable through write_stdin, read_output, and kill_command for the lifetime of the Re-CTM server process.
Any documented Re-CTM differences are security-boundary adaptations rather than missing CTM lifecycle functionality.
